mainTopic: איסור כולל and an oath on already-forbidden food, and why the משנה of one eating with many offerings leaves out a שבועה
overview: The amud begins by finishing the rejection of a proof. An oath that names forbidden food makes that food significant, but a plain oath 'not to eat' does not. רבא explains that the view accepting an איסור כולל compares it to an איסור מוסיף. The exempting view answers that an איסור מוסיף works only on one single piece. רבא then rules that a second שבועה on figs and grapes also takes hold on the figs. This teaches that איסור כולל works even for a prohibition a person makes himself. רבא בריה דרבה objects from a משנה that lists four חטאות and one אשם for a single act of eating. If איסור כולל works, an oath on dates and חלב should have made five. The גמרא gives several answers for why the משנה leaves out the שבועה: it is self-made, it can be undone by a חכם, it brings a קרבן עולה ויורד, it applies to less than a שיעור, or it is only a לאו. Each answer is tested against items on the list, like הקדש and the טמא who ate קודש. The amud ends with a challenge to the last answer: the אשם is listed even though its sin is only a לאו.

steps.title: Naming the forbidden food made it significant, but a plain oath did not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes pushing away an attempted proof. In the earlier case the person gave the forbidden food significance. In our case he did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: [There, he] gave [it] significance. But here, did he give it significance?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a rejection of a proof. It says the earlier case is different because there the person made the forbidden food important, and here he did not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When an oath mentions forbidden food directly, the person has treated that food as something worth eating, so eating it counts as 'eating.' Our case is a general oath 'not to eat' followed by eating forbidden food. Nobody made that food significant, so the earlier case cannot prove anything about this one.

keyTerms.meaning: He made it significant, treating it as something that counts
But, however (here it marks the contrast)
Here, in our case

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not say forbidden food is never 'food.' It says only that an oath which specifically names it gives it importance, and a plain oath does not.

phrases.english: [There] he gave [it] significance;
phrases.notes: This sentence starts on the line before. Some versions have the spelling in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected spelling.

phrases.english: but here, did he give it significance?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the attempted proof from the previous discussion by showing that the two cases are different.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the case of an oath that names forbidden food as proof for a plain oath not to eat.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the proof case the person made the forbidden food significant; in our case he did not.

steps.title: רבא asks the reason behind the inclusive-prohibition view
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks why the view that holds of איסור כולל lets a new prohibition take hold where one already exists.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is the reason of the one who holds of an inclusive prohibition?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new question and sets up his own answer in the next step. He wants the logic of the view that an איסור כולל can take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule that a prohibition cannot take hold where another prohibition already exists. One view says an איסור כולל is an exception: it takes hold because it also covers new, permitted items. רבא asks what that exception is built on.

keyTerms.meaning: An inclusive prohibition: it forbids new items to the same person along with the already-forbidden one
What is the reason?
Who holds of it, who accepts it

phrases.english: Rava said:
What is the reason of the one who holds of
an inclusive prohibition?
phrases.notes: The oath not to eat covers all food, so it 'includes' the forbidden food along with permitted food.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּמַאן דְּאִית לֵיהּ אִיסּוּר כּוֹלֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new line of discussion about how the oath takes hold on forbidden food.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logical basis for saying an inclusive prohibition takes effect on top of an existing prohibition.

steps.title: It is just like an added prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that איסור כולל works the same way as איסור מוסיף, which is accepted as taking effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is just like the case of an added prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own question by comparing איסור כולל to a similar, accepted rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An איסור מוסיף adds new people for whom the item becomes forbidden, and it takes hold even though the item was already forbidden to others. רבא argues that a prohibition adding new items should work in the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: It is just like, comparable to
An added prohibition: it makes the item forbidden to more people

steps.whyThisMatters: This comparison is the whole basis of the inclusive-prohibition view, and the next steps test it.

phrases.english: It is just like an added prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question from step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: איסור כולל takes effect by comparison to איסור מוסיף, which is accepted as taking effect.

steps.title: Why does the exempting view reject this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the opinion that exempts does not accept איסור כולל, if the comparison to איסור מוסיף is so strong.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who exempts, why does he not hold of it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the view that exempts, רבי שמעון in the משנה. If he accepts איסור מוסיף, why not איסור כולל? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's comparison seems to force everyone to accept איסור כולל. So the גמרא needs to explain how the exempting opinion can accept one and reject the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempts from liability
Who does not hold of it

phrases.english: And the one who exempts, why does he not hold of it?
phrases.notes: The one who exempts is רבי שמעון, who in the משנה says the person is not liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבא's comparison against the opposing opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that exempts in the case of איסור כולל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If איסור מוסיף takes effect and איסור כולל is just like it, the exempting opinion should also accept איסור כולל.

steps.title: Added prohibition works only on one single piece
steps.stepSummary: The exempting view says איסור מוסיף works on a single piece of food, but not when the new prohibition spreads to separate pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he says an added prohibition takes effect, that is on one piece. With two pieces we do not say so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the two rules are not really alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An איסור מוסיף adds more people to the very same piece of food, so the prohibition stays on one object. An איסור כולל spreads to other, separate pieces, such as permitted food together with forbidden food. The exempting view holds that this kind of spreading does not let the prohibition take hold on the already-forbidden piece.

keyTerms.meaning: One single piece
Two separate pieces
We do not say (this rule does not apply)

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides accept איסור מוסיף. They argue over איסור כולל. One side compares the two rules, and the exempting side splits them: adding people to one piece works, but spreading to separate pieces does not.

phrases.english: When he says an added prohibition [takes effect] –
that is with one single piece;
with two pieces, we do not say [so].

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אָמַר אִיסּוּר מוֹסִיף בַּחֲדָא חֲתִיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the two cases (one piece versus separate pieces)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since איסור מוסיף takes effect, איסור כולל should too.
steps.terutzMaskana: איסור מוסיף works because it stays on one piece. איסור כולל spreads across separate pieces, so the exempting view does not apply it.

steps.title: A second oath on figs and grapes also catches the figs
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that, according to the view that accepts איסור כולל, a second שבועה covering figs and grapes takes hold on the figs too, because it takes hold on the grapes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: According to the one who holds of איסור כולל, if a person said 'I swear I will not eat figs,' and then said 'I swear I will not eat figs and grapes,' since the oath takes hold on the grapes, it also takes hold on the figs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new ruling. He applies the idea of איסור כולל to a case of two oaths.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The figs are already forbidden by the first שבועה, so normally a second oath on them would have nothing to grab. But the second oath is brand new for the grapes, so it takes hold there. Since it takes hold on the grapes, it takes hold on the figs as well, just as an איסור כולל spreads to things already forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath; here, an oath forbidding oneself to eat something
Since; because it works in one place, it works in the other too
It takes hold / takes effect
And then he went back and said

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the איסור כולל idea is not limited to prohibitions from the תורה. It also applies to prohibitions a person creates through a שבועה.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
According to the one who holds of an inclusive prohibition,
if one said, 'An oath that I will not eat figs,'
and then went back and said,
'An oath that I will not eat figs and grapes,'
since the oath takes hold on the grapes,
it also takes hold on the figs.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: לְמַאן דְּאִית לֵיהּ אִיסּוּר כּוֹלֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the איסור כולל principle discussed in the earlier steps to a new case of two oaths.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the view that accepts איסור כולל, a second שבועה on figs and grapes also takes hold on the figs, which were already forbidden by the first שבועה.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא needed to say this, since it seems to follow simply from איסור כולל.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's ruling as too obvious to need saying. This sets up the next step, which explains what new point רבא is teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we already accept איסור כולל, it seems clear that it should work here too. So the גמרא wants to know what new lesson רבא's statement adds.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (asking why something needed to be said)

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether רבא's ruling in step 6 adds anything new.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the second שבועה takes hold on the figs
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If איסור כולל is accepted, applying it to oaths seems automatic, so the statement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: A prohibition a person creates still counts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that we might have thought איסור כולל works only for prohibitions that come by themselves, not for ones a person makes. רבא teaches that it works for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: for a prohibition that comes by itself we say it, but for a prohibition that a person brings on himself we do not say it. So רבא teaches us that we do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'obvious' challenge. It shows the mistake רבא's ruling prevents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A prohibition from the תורה, like not eating forbidden food, comes on its own. A שבועה is a prohibition the person creates himself. One might think איסור כולל only works for the first kind, so רבא teaches that it also works for oaths.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introducing a mistaken thought)
A prohibition that comes by itself, like a Torah prohibition
A prohibition a person brings on himself, like through an oath
He teaches us (that the mistaken thought is wrong)

steps.confusionAlert: מֵאֵלָיו and מֵעַצְמוֹ sound alike, but here they are opposites. מֵאֵלָיו is a prohibition that comes on its own, and מֵעַצְמוֹ is one the person makes himself.
steps.whatToRemember: איסור כולל applies even to prohibitions a person creates through a שבועה, not only to prohibitions from the תורה.

phrases.english: You might have said:
for a prohibition that comes by itself, we say it,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the rule of an inclusive prohibition taking hold.

phrases.english: but for a prohibition that comes from the person himself, we do not say it;
so he teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: identifies a reasonable mistake the ruling comes to prevent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: איסור כולל might work only for prohibitions that come by themselves, not for prohibitions a person creates through a שבועה.
steps.terutzMaskana: איסור כולל works for self-made prohibitions like oaths too.

steps.title: A challenge from one act of eating with four sin-offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבא בריה דרבה brings a משנה: one act of eating can make a person liable for four חטאות and one אשם, in the case of a טמא person eating חלב that is נותר from קדשים on יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא, son of רבה, raised an objection: There is a case where a person eats one time and is liable for four sin-offerings and one guilt-offering. These are the details: an impure person who ate forbidden fat, and it was leftover sacrificial meat, from the holy offerings, on יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge begins. רבא בריה דרבה quotes a משנה, and the point of his objection is laid out next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this משנה, many prohibitions pile up on one bite: eating while טמא, חלב, נותר, and eating on יום הכפורים. That makes four חטאות, plus an אשם for misusing holy property. This case of stacked prohibitions is being set up to test the earlier discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin-offerings brought for doing a forbidden act by mistake
A guilt-offering; here for misusing holy property
Forbidden fat of an animal
Sacrificial meat left past its allowed time
Holy things, animals set aside as offerings

phrases.english: Rava, son of Rabba, raised an objection:
There is one who eats a single act of eating,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in כריתות 13b.

phrases.aramaic: וְחַיָּיב עָלֶיהָ אַרְבַּע חַטָּאוֹת וְאָשָׁם אֶחָד;
phrases.english: and is liable for it four sin-offerings and one guilt-offering;
and these are they:
an impure person who ate forbidden fat,
and it was leftover sacrificial meat,
from the holy offerings,
on Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new objection from a משנה, testing the discussion of prohibitions taking hold on top of each other.
steps.kashyaTarget: The discussion of when a new prohibition can take hold where one already exists
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה shows many prohibitions stacking on one act of eating. The exact point of the objection is spelled out in what follows.

steps.title: The end of the quoted משנה: רבי מאיר adds carrying on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה. רבי מאיר adds that if it was שבת and he carried the food out, he is liable for that too. The חכמים answer that this is not the same kind of prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: Also, if it was שבת and he carried it out, he is liable. They said to him: That is not of the same type.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of the משנה it started in step 9. This sets up the real challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed four חטאות and one אשם from one act of eating. רבי מאיר wants to add a חטאת for carrying on שבת. The חכמים reject it because carrying is not an eating prohibition, and the list is only about prohibitions broken by eating.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying from one domain to another on שבת
It is not of the same type (not an eating prohibition)
Liable (here, to bring a קרבן)

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
Also, if it was Shabbat
and he carried it out, he is liable.
They said to him: It is not of the same type.
phrases.notes: Every other item on the list is broken by eating. Carrying is a different kind of prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אַף אִם הָיְתָה שַׁבָּת וְהוֹצִיאוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה that רבא בריה דרבה began quoting in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר adds liability for carrying on שבת. The חכמים say it does not count because it is not an eating prohibition.

steps.title: If איסור כולל works, the משנה could have listed five
steps.stepSummary: רבא בריה דרבה argues that if איסור כולל works, the משנה could have added a fifth liability: a שבועה not to eat dates and חלב. Since the משנה did not list it, it seems איסור כולל does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is so, you could find five, such as where he said: 'An oath that I will not eat dates and חלב.' Since the oath takes hold on the dates, it also takes hold on the חלב!
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the actual challenge from the משנה. If an oath covering dates and חלב can take hold on the חלב, the משנה should have counted it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dates are permitted, so an oath can take hold on them. Through איסור כולל, the oath should also take hold on the already-forbidden חלב. Then the same act of eating would bring one more liability. The משנה stops at four חטאות and one אשם, which suggests איסור כולל does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: You could find it (a case like this)
Dates
Since (since it works here, it works there too)
It takes hold, takes effect

steps.confusionAlert: The dates are not part of the forbidden meal. They are there only so the oath can take hold on something permitted, and then spread to the חלב.

phrases.english: And if it is so,
phrases.notes: If איסור כולל really works, as in רבא's ruling in step 6.

phrases.english: you could find five,
such as where he said
"An oath that I will not eat dates and forbidden fat,"
since the oath takes hold on the dates,
it also takes hold on the forbidden fat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה quoted in steps 9-10 to attack איסור כולל.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling (steps 6 and 8) that איסור כולל works even for a שבועה a person makes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If איסור כולל works, the משנה's list of liabilities from one act of eating should include a fifth one, a שבועה on dates and חלב. The משנה leaves it out.

steps.title: The משנה lists only prohibitions that come by themselves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה only lists prohibitions that come on their own. A שבועה is something a person makes, so the משנה did not include it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it teaches, it teaches a prohibition that comes on its own. A prohibition that a person makes himself, it does not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends איסור כולל. The משנה left out the שבועה because of the kind of list it was making, not because the שבועה would fail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלב, נותר, טומאה and יום הכפורים are all prohibitions from the תורה that apply without anyone doing anything. A שבועה exists only because a person chose to make one. The משנה chose to list only the first kind, so leaving out the שבועה proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition that comes on its own
A prohibition that comes by the person himself (he creates it)
It (the משנה) teaches

steps.confusionAlert: מֵאֵלָיו and מֵעַצְמוֹ look almost the same. Here מֵאֵלָיו means it happens on its own, and מֵעַצְמוֹ means the person himself causes it.

phrases.english: When it teaches,
it teaches a prohibition that comes on its own;
a prohibition that a person brings about himself, it does not teach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the משנה's list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leaving out a שבועה shows that איסור כולל does not work.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only lists prohibitions that come on their own, so a man-made שבועה was never meant to be on the list.

steps.title: But the משנה does list הקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. The משנה's list includes הקדש (the אשם for misusing holy property), and הקדש only comes about when a person sanctifies something.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is הקדש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. The משנה does include one prohibition that comes from a person's act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אשם in the משנה is for מעילה, eating holy property. Something becomes holy only when a person makes it הקדש, so this prohibition does not come on its own. That seems to break the rule from step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: Property a person has made holy
But look, there is
Misusing holy property, which requires an אשם

phrases.english: But there is consecrated property!
phrases.notes: This is the אשם on the משנה's list, for eating holy food. It is holy only because a person made it holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה lists only prohibitions that come on their own.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הקדש is on the משנה's list even though it exists only because a person sanctified the item, so the משנה does include a man-made prohibition.

steps.title: The case is a firstborn animal, holy from birth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge about הקדש. The משנה is talking about a בכור, which becomes holy by itself at birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is a firstborn animal, whose holiness comes from the womb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 13. The הקדש in the משנה is a בכור, and nobody had to sanctify it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 argued that הקדש also comes about through a person's act, just like a שבועה. The answer is that a בכור is holy automatically from birth. So the rule from Step 12 still stands: the משנה only lists prohibitions that come on their own.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male animal, which is holy from birth
Its holiness comes from the womb, meaning it is holy automatically at birth

phrases.english: With a firstborn animal,
phrases.notes: He means the משנה's case is about a firstborn animal, so the holy meat being eaten is from a בכור.

phrases.english: whose holiness is from the womb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13 by narrowing the case of the משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Placing the case in a specific situation (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The הקדש in the משנה was created by a person sanctifying it, so it is like a שבועה
steps.terutzMaskana: The הקדש is a בכור, holy by itself from birth, so it fits the rule of prohibitions that come on their own

steps.title: Second answer: the משנה lists only things that cannot be undone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a different answer to Step 11. The משנה only lists prohibitions that cannot be undone by asking a חכם, and a שבועה can be undone that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say this instead: when the משנה teaches its list, it includes only things that cannot be undone by asking a חכם. A שבועה, which can be undone by asking a חכם, is not taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to explain why the משנה left out the שבועה. The משנה only lists prohibitions that are permanent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer does not depend on whether a person created the prohibition. The new reason is that a שבועה can be cancelled through שאלה, so it is not a fixed prohibition like the others in the list. Either way, the missing שבועה does not prove that איסור כולל fails.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say this instead. It introduces a second answer.
Asking a חכם to release a vow or oath, which cancels it
Things, matters
It teaches, meaning the משנה lists it

phrases.english: If you want, say:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָתָנֵי, מִידֵּי דְּלֵית לֵיהּ שְׁאֵלָה;
phrases.english: when it teaches, it teaches things that cannot be undone by asking;
phrases.notes: Literally, 'things that have no asking.' You can't go to a חכם and have them cancelled.

phrases.english: an oath, which can be undone by asking,
it does not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: כִּי קָתָנֵי, מִידֵּי דְּלֵית לֵיהּ שְׁאֵלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent answer to the question of Step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining what kind of prohibition the משנה lists
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה should have listed the שבועה if איסור כולל works
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists only prohibitions that cannot be cancelled by שאלה, so a שבועה is left out

steps.title: But הקדש can also be undone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second answer. The משנה lists הקדש, and הקדש can also be cancelled by asking a חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is הקדש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 15. The משנה includes הקדש, which can be undone through שאלה, just like a שבועה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said the משנה only lists things that cannot be cancelled. A person who sanctified something can go to a חכם and have it released. So הקדש seems to break the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, there is. It introduces a counterexample.
Holy property belonging to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: But there is consecrated property!
phrases.notes: The משנה's אשם is for misusing holy property, and holy property can be released by a חכם just like a vow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule proposed in Step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה lists only prohibitions that cannot be undone by שאלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הקדש is listed in the משנה, yet it can be released through שאלה, so the rule does not fit the משנה's own list

steps.title: We already said the case is a בכור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה was already set in the case of a בכור. A בכור is holy from birth and cannot be undone by asking a חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't we already set the case as a firstborn animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 16 by pointing back to Step 14. The הקדש in the משנה is a בכור, which cannot be cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since nobody sanctified the בכור, there is no act of sanctifying to undo through שאלה. So the הקדש in the משנה fits the rule from Step 15. The second answer stands, and the missing שבועה does not prove that איסור כולל fails.

keyTerms.meaning: We have set it up, meaning we already placed the case in a specific situation

steps.whatToRemember: Both answers explain why the משנה leaves out a שבועה: either it lists only prohibitions that come on their own, or it lists only ones that cannot be undone by שאלה. In both answers, the הקדש in the משנה is a בכור. So this משנה does not disprove איסור כולל.
steps.confusionAlert: Step 15 is a separate answer from Step 12. When Step 15 is challenged, the גמרא borrows the בכור case from Step 14 to save it.

phrases.english: Didn't we already set it up with a firstborn animal?
phrases.notes: This points back to Step 14. A בכור was never sanctified by a person, so there is nothing for a חכם to undo.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16 by applying the setup of Step 14 to the second answer
steps.terutzResolutionType: Using the earlier setting of the case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The הקדש in the משנה can be undone by שאלה, which breaks the rule
steps.terutzMaskana: The הקדש is a בכור, which cannot be undone by שאלה, so the rule holds

steps.title: The משנה only lists sins with a fixed offering
steps.stepSummary: Another answer to Step 11: the משנה lists only sins that carry a קרבן קבוע. Breaking a שבועה carries a קרבן עולה ויורד, so it is not listed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say this: when the משנה teaches its list, it teaches sins with a fixed offering. It does not teach sins with a sliding-scale offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more answer to why the משנה leaves out a שבועה. The משנה only counts sins that need a fixed offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answers looked at whether the prohibition depends on a person or can be undone by a חכם. This answer looks at the type of קרבן instead. Every item in the list carries a קרבן קבוע, while breaking a שבועה carries a קרבן עולה ויורד, which depends on how much money the sinner has. So a שבועה simply does not belong in this list.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: introduces another possible answer
A fixed offering: the same animal no matter how rich or poor the sinner is
A sliding-scale offering: animal, birds, or flour, depending on what the person can afford

steps.confusionAlert: This does not say a broken שבועה brings no קרבן. It does bring one, but a different kind (עולה ויורד), so it falls outside this list.

phrases.english: If you want, say:
when he teaches, it is a fixed offering;
a sliding-scale offering he does not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: כִּי קָתָנֵי, קׇרְבָּן קָבוּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new, independent answer to the question of Step 11, alongside the answers in Steps 12 and 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the scope of the משנה's list by the type of קרבן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A broken שבועה should have been listed as one more liability for the same act of eating.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists only sins with a קרבן קבוע, so a שבועה, which carries a קרבן עולה ויורד, is left out.

steps.title: But an impure person eating holy food brings a sliding-scale offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 18: the משנה lists a טמא who ate קודש, and that sin carries a קרבן עולה ויורד.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look, the משנה lists an impure person who ate holy food, and that sin carries a sliding-scale offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. The משנה itself lists a sin that carries a sliding-scale offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 claimed the list holds only sins with a fixed offering. But one item on the list is a טמא eating קודש, and that sin normally carries a קרבן עולה ויורד. So the rule from Step 18 seems to be broken by the משנה itself.

keyTerms.meaning: But look: points to something that seems to contradict
An impure person who ate holy sacrificial food

phrases.english: But there is an impure person who ate holy food –
which is a sliding-scale offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 18 using an item in the משנה itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה lists only sins with a קרבן קבוע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה includes טמא שאכל את הקודש, whose קרבן is עולה ויורד, so the list is not limited to fixed offerings.

steps.title: The משנה is about a king, following רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is describing a נשיא. According to רבי אליעזר, a נשיא who ate קודש while impure brings a שעיר, which is a fixed offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is about a king, and it follows רבי אליעזר, who says a king brings a male goat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The person in the משנה is a נשיא, and for him the offering is fixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a regular person, eating קודש while טמא carries a קרבן עולה ויורד. But רבי אליעזר holds that a נשיא brings a שעיר instead, which is a קרבן קבוע. If the משנה is about a נשיא and follows רבי אליעזר, every item stays fixed, and the answer of Step 18 holds.

keyTerms.meaning: The king (the highest leader)
A male goat brought as a חטאת

phrases.english: It is about a king, and it is רבי אליעזר,
who says: a king brings a male goat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19 by defining the case as a נשיא, following רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case (a נשיא) and assigns the משנה to a specific opinion (רבי אליעזר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The טמא in the משנה brings a קרבן עולה ויורד, which breaks the rule of Step 18.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a נשיא, who according to רבי אליעזר brings a fixed שעיר, so every item on the list carries a fixed offering.

steps.title: The משנה only lists prohibitions that need a minimum amount
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives another answer: the משנה lists only things that need a שיעור. A שבועה can take effect even on less than a שיעור, so it is not listed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: when he teaches, it is things that need a minimum amount. An oath, which can take effect on less than the minimum amount, he does not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a completely new answer to why the משנה leaves out a שבועה. The answer is about the minimum amount eaten, not about the type of offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the prohibitions in the משנה apply only when a person eats a set minimum amount, a שיעור. A שבועה is different, because it can take effect even on eating less than a שיעור. Since a שבועה does not follow the same amount rule as the rest of the list, the משנה leaves it out.

keyTerms.meaning: A set minimum amount needed to be liable
Takes effect
Less than the minimum amount

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא gives several separate answers for why a שבועה is not in the משנה's list: it depends on a person, it can be undone by a חכם, it carries a קרבן עולה ויורד, and (רב אשי) it can take effect on less than a שיעור. Step 24 adds one more answer.

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
when he teaches, it is things that need a minimum amount;

phrases.aramaic: שְׁבוּעָה דְּחָיְילָא אַפָּחוֹת מִכְּשִׁיעוּר, לָא קָתָנֵי.
phrases.english: an oath, which takes effect on less than the minimum amount, he does not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: כִּי קָתָנֵי, מִידֵּי דְּבָעֵי שִׁיעוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another independent answer to the question of Step 11, separate from the קרבן קבוע approach of Steps 18-20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the scope of the משנה's list by the minimum amount needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A broken שבועה should have been listed as one more liability for the same act of eating.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists only prohibitions that need a שיעור. A שבועה can take effect on less than a שיעור, so it is left out.

steps.title: What about consecrated property?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's answer by pointing to הקדש, which is listed in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about consecrated property? It is in the list!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's answer from Step 21. It points to הקדש, which is in the משנה's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said the משנה lists only things that need a שיעור. The challenge assumes that misusing הקדש makes a person liable even for less than a כזית. If that is true, the משנה does list something with no שיעור, so why not list שבועה too?

keyTerms.meaning: But look at...; used to point to a case that seems to contradict
Property set aside as holy, belonging to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: But what about consecrated property!
phrases.notes: He means: the משנה lists misusing holy property, and that seems to apply even to less than a כזית.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אשי's answer in Step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's rule that the משנה lists only things that need a שיעור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הקדש is listed, yet it seems to apply even to less than a כזית, so lacking a שיעור should not keep שבועה off the list.

steps.title: Consecrated property needs a פרוטה's worth
steps.stepSummary: הקדש does have a minimum amount: a שוה פרוטה of benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need the value of a פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אשי. It says that הקדש really does have a minimum amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person is liable for misusing הקדש only when he gets benefit worth at least a פרוטה. So הקדש fits the rule: it needs a שיעור. It is just counted in money, not in size like a כזית. רב אשי's answer still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: We require
The value of a פרוטה, the smallest coin; the minimum amount for liability

phrases.english: But we require the value of a perutah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: הקדש does have a שיעור, measured in money
steps.terutzHavaAmina: הקדש has no minimum amount, so it breaks רב אשי's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: הקדש needs a שוה פרוטה, so it is a thing with a שיעור, and רב אשי's rule holds.
steps.whatToRemember: A שיעור does not have to be a size like a כזית. For הקדש the minimum amount is a value: a שוה פרוטה.

steps.title: The list covers only sins punished by כרת
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא gives a new answer: the משנה lists only sins whose deliberate version is punished with כרת. Breaking a שבועה on purpose is only a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אשי of Avireya said that רבי זירא said: When the משנה teaches its list, it teaches cases where doing the sin on purpose brings כרת. Cases where doing it on purpose is only a לאו, it does not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: A new answer is given to why שבועה is not in the list. The משנה lists only sins that are punished with כרת when done on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a fresh reason that does not depend on שיעור at all. Someone who breaks a שבועה on purpose gets lashes for a לאו, not כרת. So שבועה is a different kind of sin and is left out of the list.

keyTerms.meaning: From Avireya, a place; this tells us which רב אשי this is
Doing it on purpose (deliberately)
Being cut off, a punishment from Heaven
A negative commandment; breaking it on purpose usually brings lashes
He (the משנה) teaches

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same רב אשי as in Step 21. This one is רב אשי from Avireya, quoting רבי זירא, and he gives a completely different reason.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב אָשֵׁי מֵאַוֵּירְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: And Rav Ashi of Avireya said that Rabbi Zeira said:
When it teaches, it is cases where doing it on purpose brings karet;
cases where doing it on purpose is only a negative commandment, it does not teach.
phrases.notes: Breaking a שבועה on purpose is only a לאו, so by this rule it stays off the list.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב אָשֵׁי מֵאַוֵּירְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another answer to the original question of Step 11, alongside the answers in Steps 12, 15, 18 and 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining what the list includes: only sins whose deliberate version carries כרת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה should list every sin that brings a קרבן, including breaking a שבועה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists only sins punished with כרת when done on purpose. Breaking a שבועה is only a לאו, so it is left out.

steps.title: But אשם is listed and it is only a לאו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא: the אשם for misusing הקדש is in the list, yet doing that sin on purpose is only a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the guilt offering, where doing the sin on purpose is only a negative commandment, and the משנה teaches it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי זירא's answer from Step 24. It points to the אשם, which is in the list even though its sin is only a לאו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא said the משנה lists only sins punished with כרת. But misusing הקדש, which brings an אשם, is only a לאו when done on purpose, and it is still listed. So the rule seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A guilt offering; here, the one brought for misusing הקדש
Whose deliberate version

phrases.english: But what about the guilt offering, where doing it on purpose is only a negative commandment,
phrases.notes: This is the אשם brought for misusing הקדש, the same case from Step 22.

phrases.english: and it teaches it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 24
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's rule that the משנה lists only sins punished with כרת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The אשם for misusing הקדש is in the list, yet that sin done on purpose is only a לאו. So the list does include a לאו, and that reason cannot explain why שבועה is left out.
